B001.notes: The complete printed proposition binds arbitrary X, EMetricSpace, MeasurableSpace and BorelSpace instances, then real s and arbitrary A; its result is exactly equality with the supremum over positive ENNReal scales of the header's Content. Unfolding Content gives precisely the same countable cover infima and nonempty-member guarded costs as the source. Empty-member costs are zero for all s; removing the guard is justified here only for s>0, as the rewritten argument specifies. There is no spherical restriction or normalization factor. The original positive-exponent cover definition in problem.md:34–47 is preserved.
B001.source: Pinned Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/Hausdorff.lean:535–552 defines hausdorffMeasure s as mkMetric (r ↦ r^s) and proves hausdorffMeasure_apply with exactly these infima, supremum and guards. Its Borel assumptions occur at 442–444. The submitted proof is direct application after the definitional abbreviation Content; the supplied actual_type retains all these assumptions. Origin evidence/documents are empty; the declaration was independently read using the fixed Mathlib tool, which is the declared revision reference.
B001.application: Used in definitions/normalization and §1 (B101) to identify the measure with the scale-content supremum; §2/§3 use that internal consequence. The spaces at the final application are ordinary Euclidean and maximum-product metric spaces, equipped with their Borel structures; an arbitrary intermediate metric space can likewise be given its Borel structure. No measurability of A or covering members is needed. Restriction from extended scales to finite positive real scales is explicitly an internal reduction, not attributed to this leaf.
